subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept the bounded longer isolated-cron setup window in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219, require a tighter cap, or require an operator-configurable watchdog instead?
rationale: Current main still has the 60s bug, but fixing it changes how long a genuinely stuck isolated setup can occupy cron capacity, which is a maintainer-owned availability tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Land the open PR or equivalent behavior so long isolated setup can use part of the job timeout budget while staying capped.

options.title: Tighten the cap before merge
options.body: Ask the fix PR to use a lower maximum setup window if cron-slot occupancy is more important than slow-host recovery.

options.title: Require an explicit config knob
options.body: Pause the derived-default fix and require a documented operator setting for deployments that need a longer setup watchdog.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Land the open PR or equivalent behavior so long isolated setup can use part of the job timeout budget while staying capped.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the cron watchdog owner boundary and default availability tradeoff, and steipete authored the refactor that made agent-watchdog.ts the current owner module.
